summary: Round 3 ran without a PI (the PI process failed), so both students worked the open frontier autonomously and INDEPENDENTLY CONVERGED on a result that OVERTURNS my round-1/2 'gate'. This round I rebuilt the oracle from my own bg.cpp and re-verified the corrected load-bearing claim end-to-end with my own exact-rational analysis (no student code). CONFIRMED: the three-minus sector is piecewise-RATIONAL, NOT piecewise-polynomial. A_n^{3-} = i*2^{n-1}*g^{3-n} * N_n(omega) / D_n, with D_n = prod_{i in minus, j in plus}(omega_i+omega_j) the product of all 3(n-3) mixed-pair frequency SUMS (minimal by symmetry), and N_n a continuous SPLINE (deg 5n-13, S_3 wr Z_2-symmetric, odd under omega->-omega). A_n is finite everywhere (no factorization poles) yet rational; the (omega_i+omega_j)=0 loci are shielded chamber walls (kink, not pole). The open problem is now precisely the explicit closed form for the spline numerator N_n. Not SOLVED -- no SOLVED.md. Assigned two complementary attacks on N_n.

reverification.oracle: Rebuilt bots/pi/code/bg from my own bg.cpp copy (g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -lgmpxx -lgmp). Anchors: n=5 w=2,3,5 -> -25344 i; one-minus -> 0; n=6, n=7 finite.
reverification.rational_not_polynomial: bots/pi/code/pi_r4_denominator.py (own slice construction, own exact Lagrange + rational reconstruction). On a clean one-chamber F-constant slice, A_6/i is NOT polynomial up to degree 25 -> rational. OVERTURNS my round-2 'piecewise-polynomial' gate.
reverification.denominator_D9_clears: (A_6/i)*D_9 IS an exact polynomial on the slice (deg 20 there); confirmed in 3 distinct chamber/ordering pieces (pi_r4_spline.py).
reverification.sums_of_squares_fail: (A_6/i)*prod(omega_i^2+omega_j^2) is NOT polynomial -> the denominator is frequency SUMS, not sums of squares.
reverification.reduced_denominator_divides_D9: Exact rational reconstruction of A_6/i gives reduced P/Q with deg Q=4; Q DIVIDES D_9 (its roots are mixed-pair frequency-sum zeros).
reverification.minimality: Combinatorial: the S_3(minus) x S_3(plus) orbit of one mixed pair is the full 9-element set, so the only symmetric divisors of D_9 are 1 and D_9; since A_n is not polynomial, reduced symmetric denominator = D_9 (minimal).
reverification.spline_numerator: bots/pi/code/pi_r4_spline2.py: crossing the MIXED wall omega_2=omega_4 (k_{2,4}=0, D_9 != 0) on an F-const slice, N_6 is a DIFFERENT polynomial each side (deg 20 vs 18 on slice) but CONTINUOUS at the wall -> A_6 continuous = kink, not pole; so A_n is rational PER CHAMBER, not one global rational function. The plus-plus ordering omega_4=omega_5 is analytic (same polynomial both sides) -> kinks live on the MIXED {k_S=0} walls.
reverification.n5_control: Same test on n=5 returns 'polynomial' (degree 2 on the slice) directly -> method sound; the n=6 'rational' verdict is genuine.
reverification.n7_spot_check: A_7/i rational; (A_7/i)*D_12 (12 mixed pairs) IS polynomial on a slice -> the all-n denominator form holds.

gate_correction: Round-1/2 conclusion 'three-minus is piecewise-POLYNOMIAL (no poles)' was WRONG on the polynomial part. 'No factorization poles' is correct but does NOT imply polynomial: a ratio whose denominator never vanishes on the physical region is finite everywhere yet rational. Correct statement: piecewise-RATIONAL with explicit minimal common denominator D_n and spline numerator N_n. The degree-8 homogeneity I verified earlier is consistent with the rational form (deg N_6 - deg D_9 = 17 - 9 = 8).
reconciliation: This reconciles the round-2 student split: the box-spline / truncated-power object the team hunted lives in the polynomial NUMERATOR N_n, not in A_n. Both pictures were right about different objects. Cross-validation now triple-independent (student-1 s1_008, student-2 s2_010, PI round 4).
